00125 /**
00126  * @brief               Set application window resizing behavior
00127  *
00128  * An application can call this function before calling HxUiInit to set the
00129  * application's behavior with regards to screen dimension changes.  The
00130  * default behavior, equivalent to calling HxUiApplicationWindowResizes(false),
00131  * is for the application window to stay at the LCD screen size.
00132  *
00133  * After a call to HxUiApplicationWindowResizes(true), the application window
00134  * will resize to match the size of the screen, which can change if the user
00135  * has hooked up the device to a projector or monitor.  Applications should
00136  * listen for the kHxAppWindowResized message, or register a callback for the
00137  * kHxPropertyScreenDimension notification to know when the window is resized.
00138  *
00139  * This API should be called before your program's call to HxUiInit as it will
00140  * affect the size of the application window created by HxUiInit.  Changing
00141  * this value after the program starts will not affect the system behavior.
00142  *
00143  * @param resizeOnScreenChange  IN:     If set to true, application window 
00144  *                                      resizes when the screen size changes;
00145  *                                      if false, the application window has
00146  *                                      a fixed size.
00147  *
00148  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK on success.  
00149  */
00150 HxResult HxUiApplicationWindowResizes(bool resizeOnScreenChange);

00170 /**
00171  * @brief               Set mode of event loop
00172  *
00173  * This function changes how events are processed by HxWindowEventLoop.
00174  *
00175  * By default, HxWindowEventLoop exits when its timeout expires, or as a
00176  * result of the deletion of the app window.
00177  *
00178  * If the exitIfIdle argument of this function is set to true,
00179  * HxWindowEventLoop exits prior to the expiration of the timeout if the
00180  * event queue is empty.   
00181  *
00182  * If you find yourself wanting this function, you should look at
00183  * using HxWindowSetIdleCallback instead, as that doesn't cause the
00184  * event loop to exit, it just calls a helper function when it goes
00185  * idle.
00186  *
00187  * @param exitIfIdle    IN:     If set to true, exit when idle
00188  *
00189  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK.
00190  */
00191 HxResult HxUiExitEventLoopIfIdle(bool exitIfIdle);

00194 /**
00195  * @brief               Enable or disable focus handling
00196  *
00197  * HxUiCustomFocusHandling either enables or disables the default focus
00198  * handling, or how the keyboard and/or scrollwheel is used to navigate from
00199  * widget to widget.  This API is provided for applications that need to
00200  * customize how focus is implemented.
00201  *
00202  * Note that HxUiCustomWheelHandling is used to customize scrollwheel events,
00203  * while allowing the system to handle other events.  HxUiCustomFocusHandling, 
00204  * however, disables all focus handling by the system.
00205  *
00206  * When focus handling is customized, widgets are not added to the focus
00207  * array when created.  Instead, the application uses explicit calls to
00208  * HxWidgetSetFocusArray at appropriate times to determine which widgets
00209  * are included in the focus array.
00210  *
00211  * The application is responsible for ensuring that HxWidgetSetFocusArray
00212  * is called with the valid focusable widgets after a focusable widget is
00213  * deallocated ro hidden.  Failure to do this will lead to assertions on
00214  * debug builds, and faults on release builds.
00215  *
00216  * By default, focus handling is not customized, with the system adding all
00217  * focusable widgets when they are allocated ro made visible, and removing
00218  * them from the internal array when they are deallocated or hidden.
00219  *
00220  * @param custom       IN:      If set to true, disable default focus handling
00221  *
00222  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK.
00223  */
00224 HxResult HxUiCustomFocusHandling(bool custom);
00225 
00226 
00227 /**
00228  * @brief               Customize scrollwheel handling
00229  *
00230  * HxUiCustomWheelHandling allows an application to override the default
00231  * system behavior of how scrollwheel events affect focus handling.
00232  *
00233  * The system has the following default behavior:
00234  *
00235  *      Scrollwheel with kHxKeyModifierNone: change the selection of a dropdown
00236  *      box or list that has focus, or scroll a container when the container 
00237  *      has focus.
00238  *
00239  *      Scrollwheel with kHxKeyModifierShift:  change widget focus backward
00240  *      or forward, depending on the direction the scrollwheel is moved.
00241  *
00242  * The modifier argument is a bitmask, so more than one modifier can be
00243  * customized.  Only kHxKeyModifierNone, kHxKeyModifierShift, 
00244  * kHxKeyModifierAlt and kHxKeyModifierAltGr are used by the system,
00245  * however.
00246  *
00247  * Use kHxKeyModifierNotCustom to disable all scrollwheel customization.  If
00248  * other modifier flags are combined, they are ignored, and will no longer
00249  * override default system behavior.
00250  *
00251  * HX_INVALID_ARG is returned if bits other than kHxKeyModifierNone,
00252  * kHxKeyModifierShift, kHxKeyModifierAlt, or kHxKeyModifierNotCustom are set.
00253  *
00254  * @param modifier     IN:      Bitmask modifier key 
00255  *
00256  * @return HxResult:            Returns HX_OK.  
00257  */
00258 HxResult HxUiCustomWheelHandling(HxKeyModifier_t modifier);
00259
